ownerSteering: Jared 22 November: make the unusual scientific image styles tangible. Twelfth world uses multiple-exposure movement photography of invented body-instrument performers.

prompts.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. GLAZE CHRONOPHOTOGRAPHIC ENSEMBLE, a tangible invented living orchestra studied through stroboscopic multiple-exposure photography. MEDIUM: a polished scientific CHRONOPHOTOGRAPH, continuous-tone monochrome silver-gelatin exposure with a subtle warm ivory/amber bias and fine photographic grain. ONE fully opaque, crisply resolved main instant of a real-looking invented organism is accompanied by TWO much dimmer translucent earlier exposures of the MOVING PARTS or body. Each ghost exposure is an actual recognizable anatomical position, smoothly filled continuous tone, not an outline, tracer, wireframe, particle path, light streak, chart or separate panel. The main figure has solid opaque skin/mechanism surfaces with controlled photographic shading; do not reveal skeletons or internal structures. Subtle soft side lighting, no glossy metallic specular shine or glass. Keep the solid main subject dominant; dim ghosts at about 15% and 30% intensity explain a clear mechanical or anatomical action. Slight repeated positions must fit together as ONE motion study, not three independent creatures. Not an ordinary musical instrument, routine object collection, toy render, sculpture photo, engraving, screenprint, X-ray, coloured registration, thermal map, rainbow or optical fringe. No musical notes, sound-wave symbols, text, labels, numerals, grids, clock faces, readings, graphs, logos or watermark. Asset: ONE independent square 1024x1024 pure-art widget. Subject BELLOWS BREATHER: one squat friendly organism whose large expanding thorax IS a broad concertina chamber with five thick folded ribs, a small rounded head with two recessed eye apertures, two long hinged arms pressing gently against the sides of its own thorax, two short broad split-toed feet and two curved ear-like balancing fins. It makes sound by compressing its own body, not by holding an accordion or tool. Three-quarter view. Main instant thorax partly compressed; two dim prior exposures show the arms and ribs farther apart, clearly demonstrating lateral compression. Keep one clear main face and planted feet. Whole main subject AND ALL ghost exposure positions fit fully inside central 70% of canvas with generous truly empty margins. True transparent alpha exterior and gaps between limbs/exposures. No dark rectangular backing, floor, cast shadow, haze, exterior bloom, tile, frame, panel, diagram or device mockup.
